items.title: Endoville Backend
items.text:
This is the API for the Endoville store. You use it to create accounts, browse products and posts, keep a cart, place orders, take payment, and track a shipment.

You can read the catalog and the blog without signing in. For anything else, sign in first and send the access token with the request. The get started guide walks through that once.

items.title: Responses
items.text:
Every response is JSON. If a field is wrong, the error uses that field's name. If you are not allowed to do something, or the record is missing, the error is in detail.

Status What it means 200 OK The call worked 201 Created Something new was saved 400 Bad Request A field in the body is missing or invalid 401 Unauthorized Sign in, or send a valid access token 403 Forbidden You are signed in, but you cannot do this 404 Not Found That record is not there

items.title: Architecture
items.text:
This page is a map of the backend. A shopper can register, browse, keep a cart, place an order, and pay. Staff look after the catalog, payments, and shipping. Each order has one parcel, and that parcel is what the shopper tracks.

The first half is what the API does today. The second half is the purchasing and dispatch handoff we still need to add. Those new records sit on the order line and the parcel you already have. They do not replace them.

items.title: Identity
items.text:
CustomUser (AUTH_USER_MODEL) has no username. Email and phone are each unique and nullable, and at least one is required. Accounts with an @endovillehealth.com email are created as staff.

OTP is a six-digit code for activation or login. A new code replaces the previous one for that email or phone. Verification allows three failures, then the code is rejected. Expiry comes from OTP_EXPIRY_MINUTES at send time. The model helper create_otp uses a five-minute window.

Login returns a JWT pair. Google login uses allauth and the same user model. is_staff marks a staff account. A Django admin is is_superuser and has every role. Other staff have Django groups ticked as roles: Orders, Shipping, Stock, and Manager. A new staff account from an @endovillehealth.com email starts with Orders, Shipping, and Stock. An admin adds a staff user at POST /api/users/staff/ and sends only the roles that person should have. Staff read customers and their shipping addresses at GET /api/users/customers/. Staff accounts are left out of that list. Repeated copies of one address are returned once.

Commerce permissions:

  • Orders: all orders, line changes, payments, refunds, and payment credentials. Can place an order for a customer.
  • Shipping: shipments, shipment events, and reading every order and shipment.
  • Stock: create and edit products and variants.
  • Manager: warehouse create and update. Other staff can read a warehouse and cannot change it.
  • An admin passes every role check.

Currency.usd_rate means how many units of that currency equal 1 USD. One row is is_primary. Stripe FX quotes refresh usd_rate for every active currency except USD, so a shopper price matches the amount checkout charges. rate_synced_at is the time of that quote. Order totals are stored in the primary currency. A payment stores the usd_rate it was charged with, and Order.recalculate_is_fully_paid converts that payment back with the stored rate.

Product is the listing: name, description, brand, price, cost price, optional stock, unit weight in grams (default 1), optional SKU, unique barcode, images, SEO slug, featured flag, and is_cancelled. track_stock defaults off. Checkout ignores stock until a stock number is set on create or edit, which turns track_stock on. Sending track_stock: false leaves the number unused. supplier_order_urls is a list of http(s) links staff use to buy that product from a supplier. Public responses omit cost_price, supplier_order_urls, and revenue. quantity_sold is public. It and revenue are stored from order lines and move with a sale, a removed line, or a cancelled or refunded order. revenue is the sum of those line totals in the primary currency, and only staff receive it. avg_rating and review_count are denormalized from reviews that are not flagged.

Brand and Category store products_count and products_sold so a list does not count rows on each request. products_count goes up or down when a product is linked or unlinked. A product in several subcategories of one category counts once. products_sold is the quantity_sold of the products linked there now. Placing a line adds the quantity. Removing or replacing a line, or cancelling or refunding the order, takes those units back off. Moving a product to another brand or category, or deleting it, moves that product's quantity_sold with it.

ProductVariant is the purchasable combination of variation options. Price and cost override the product when set. Stock does not. A variant sale reduces that variant's stock only, and only when the variant's track_stock is on. Barcode is unique when present.

ProductReview is one review per user per product, rating 0–5. Create is allowed only when the user has a completed, fully paid order with a confirmed line for that product. Unavailable and replaced lines were not shipped, so they cannot be reviewed. The order link is stored on the review. Staff cannot delete a review. They flag it as PROFANITY, MALICIOUS, or OTHER. A flagged review is hidden from other customers and dropped from avg_rating and review_count. Staff and the author still see it, including is_flagged, flag_reason, and flagged_at. The author cannot change that flag. Staff can clear it.

Public reads, staff writes: StaffWriteReadOnly on products, variants, brands, categories, currencies, and variation tables.

items.title: Listing mode to add on Product
items.text:
Each listing needs a fulfillment mode so staff know whether paid units are already at a shipping location or must be bought.

Add these fields to products.Product:

Field Type Meaning fulfillment_mode WAREHOUSE or SUPPLIER Default WAREHOUSE, so current products keep today's behavior supplier FK to orders.Supplier, null Required in practice when mode is SUPPLIER shipping_location FK to orders.ShippingLocation, null Where this product is packed and dispatched from

Do not put this on the variant unless a later listing truly splits one product across modes. A variant keeps its own stock and does not draw from the product.

stock stays "units available to sell" when track_stock is on, and checkout decrements that shelf. For WAREHOUSE, that number is on-hand at shipping_location. For SUPPLIER, it is available-to-promise: the customer can buy it, and staff must raise a supplier order for the quantity sold. Checkout does not grow a second stock counter. When track_stock is off, checkout does not read or change the number.

items.title: Content
items.text:
blogs.Category and blogs.Subcategory are separate from the product taxonomy. Author is a byline, not a CustomUser. Post has slug, excerpt, SEO fields, is_published, views, and optional related_products. Comment is written by a CustomUser on a post.

Reads are public. Creating or editing authors, categories, and posts is staff-only. Comments can be created by an authenticated user and changed by the author or staff.

items.title: Cart
items.text:
One Cart per user. CartItem is either a product or a variant, never both, and unique per cart. Sync replaces the line set and clears last_reminder_at. Clear deletes lines the same way. The cart response includes weight_grams, shipping_fee, and shipping_fees for the lines currently in the basket, using the same schedule as checkout. shipping_fee is set when the shopper sends country, when only one country is configured, or when no countries are configured and the fee is 0.00. Otherwise it is null and shipping_fees lists each country.

Abandoned-cart emails go out at 12, 24, and 48 hours of inactivity, one step on each run. last_reminder_at stays empty until an email succeeds, then stores the cart's last activity plus that step. A background task runs on ABANDONED_CART_REMINDER_BG_INTERVAL_SECONDS (default 1800). Placing an order clears the cart.

items.title: Order
items.text:
Order.status:

Status When it is set PAYMENT_PENDING Created, or the bill is no longer covered while the order is still being processed PLACED Legacy. A covered bill moves it to PROCESSING PROCESSING The bill is covered and the parcel has not left. This is the order being processed SHIPPING Shipment becomes DISPATCHED or OUT_FOR_DELIVERY. The order is being shipped COMPLETE Shipment becomes DELIVERED

is_fully_paid is the covered-bill fact. It is derived from payments and completed refunds and is not writable. It stays true through processing, shipping, and completion while the money still covers total. PROCESSING is that fact before the parcel leaves. A later shortfall moves PROCESSING back to PAYMENT_PENDING and leaves SHIPPING and COMPLETE on the parcel. Changing shipping_fee recalculates total and this paid state. | CANCELLED | Customer may cancel only their own unpaid order. Pending payments are cancelled with it | | REFUNDED | Every received payment has a completed refund record. Staff can set this status to write those refunds. The order stays REFUNDED only after every held payment is covered, and that check runs once the refund rows exist. Recording the refund does not call the payment provider |

Money fields subtotal, shipping_fee, and total are snapshotted on the order. shipping_fee is USD. Checkout sets it from the shipping country table: the destination's fee for one unit of weight, or that fee times basket weight divided by the unit weight when the basket is heavier. Weight is each line's unit_weight in grams, and a variant line uses its product. A request shipping_fee is ignored. With no country rates saved, the fee is 0.00. Once any country is saved, checkout to a country that is not on the list is refused. An admin replaces the table at PUT /api/orders/shipping-rates/ and can edit a row in Django admin. Anyone can read it and quote a basket at POST /api/orders/shipping-rates/quote/. The Orders role can still change the stored fee on an order after it is placed. ShippingAddress is its own row copied at checkout, not a live profile address.

Warehouse is the receiving address a placed order is shipped to. It is not the customer’s delivery address, and it is not created automatically. Staff read it at /api/orders/staff/warehouses/. A manager or admin creates and edits the address there. code is set on create and then fixed. Only one warehouse stays is_active. Checkout stores that active warehouse on the order. When none is active, Order.warehouse is null. Orders already placed keep the warehouse they were given. Customers see that nested address on the order and cannot edit the warehouse record.

OrderItem stores product_name, variant_description, barcode, quantity, unit_price, and line_total so catalog edits do not rewrite history. product and variant foreign keys are nullable and use SET_NULL.

Checkout in CreateOrderSerializer.create is one transaction: address, order, stock decrement, line snapshots, totals, then Shipment plus a first ShipmentEvent of ORDER_PLACED / "Order placed".

items.title: Payment
items.text:
PaymentCredentials holds the active key pair per provider and environment (sandbox or live). The secret is encrypted with a Fernet key derived from SECRET_KEY. Only one active row is kept per provider and environment.

OrderPayment is an attempt: provider, amount, currency, checkout URL, provider ids, and raw response. transaction_id is optional. Staff may omit it, send null, or send an empty string, and the stored value is null. A non-empty id must be unique. It is included on staff payment responses and on each payment inside an order. A new payment is refused when the order is CANCELLED or is_fully_paid is already true. Returning money is an OrderRefund. Any payment or refund change recomputes is_fully_paid. A covered bill moves PAYMENT_PENDING or PLACED to PROCESSING. A shortfall moves PROCESSING back to PAYMENT_PENDING. The order confirmation email is sent on commit when a payment first becomes completed.

OrderRefund is the record for returning money from a completed payment. Every refund stores a reason and a unique transaction_id. Staff send both when they create one at /api/orders/staff/refunds/ for a cancelled order, for the full balance or a smaller amount. A line change writes the reason from that change and assigns a transaction id. Payments themselves are not edited or deleted. Status initiated sets the payment to refund_initiated while any refund is still open. The order still counts that money as paid. A completed refund is subtracted from the paid sum. When completed refunds cover the payment, its status becomes refunded. When every received payment on a cancelled order is refunded, the order becomes REFUNDED. Orders include refunds next to payments.

Staff changes to an order status, a line, a payment, a refund, or a product or variant price are stored on StaffChangeLog. The row keeps the staff user, a short summary, and the before and after values. Shopper checkout and provider callbacks are left out, because those requests have no staff user. Staff read the log at GET /api/users/staff-changes/.

Each order line starts as pending. Staff confirm it (POST /api/orders/orders/{id}/items/{item_id}/confirm/), mark it unavailable (.../unavailable/, and .../remove/ does the same), or replace it (.../replace/) while the order is PAYMENT_PENDING, PLACED, or PROCESSING. An unavailable line stays on the order, drops out of subtotal and total, returns its stock, and no longer counts as a sale. A replacement keeps the original line as replaced and adds a confirmed line for the product that will ship. The customer sees both, including availability_note when staff left one. The order cannot move to SHIPPING or COMPLETE until every line is confirmed, unavailable, or replaced, and at least one line is confirmed. A lower total on a paid order writes an initiated partial refund for the difference. A review is allowed only for a confirmed line on a completed, fully paid order.

Providers in code: intasend, stripe, pesapal, cash, other. Stripe completion is the webhook POST /api/orders/payments/stripe/webhook/. Staff and the order owner can also call POST /api/orders/payments/{id}/check-status/ while a Stripe checkout is still pending. That reads the Checkout Session and marks the payment completed when Stripe says it is paid. Creating another payment first checks those open Stripe sessions, and refuses the new payment when one of them has already covered the order.

items.title: Shipment
items.text:
One Shipment per Order. Status values: ORDER_PLACED, DISPATCHED, OUT_FOR_DELIVERY, DELIVERED. Carrier, tracking number, tracking URL, and delivery timestamps live here.

Order.status and Shipment.status stay on the same step. DISPATCHED or OUT_FOR_DELIVERY keeps the order at SHIPPING. DELIVERED keeps it at COMPLETE and fills delivered_at when that timestamp is empty. Moving the order to SHIPPING or COMPLETE moves the parcel the same way, and moving either one back to placed or to PAYMENT_PENDING / PROCESSING moves the other back with it. OUT_FOR_DELIVERY is kept when the order stays on SHIPPING. Cancelled and refunded orders leave the parcel where it is. Entering SHIPPING or COMPLETE is refused while any line is still pending, or when the order has lines and none of them are confirmed. A save that does not write status does not apply these changes.

ShipmentEvent is the customer timeline: status, message, location, occurred_at. Saving an event whose status is DISPATCHED or OUT_FOR_DELIVERY moves the shipment forward to that status and sets the order to SHIPPING. A DELIVERED event moves the shipment to DELIVERED, records delivered_at when it is empty, and sets the order to COMPLETE. Events only move a shipment forward. The order and the parcel still follow the rules above once the shipment status changes.

Customers read shipments for their own orders. Staff update them at /api/orders/staff/shipments/ and append events at /api/orders/staff/shipment-events/.

items.title: Rules the fulfillment addition follows
items.text:
1. Customer tracking remains one Shipment and its events. Dispatch confirmation fills carrier, tracking_number, tracking_url, and status DISPATCHED. It does not invent a second tracking model.
  2. An order is exported only when every line is ready to pack. A half-ready order stays in PROCESSING. That matches one shipment per order. Split shipments would require changing Shipment.order from one-to-one to foreign key, which this design does not do.
  3. Supplier purchasing and dispatch batches are staff-only and live under /api/orders/staff/, same as shipment updates.
  4. Line snapshots stay immutable for name, barcode, and price. Fulfillment status is operational and may change after checkout.
  5. Catalog mode is copied onto the line at checkout. Later edits to the product do not rewrite open orders.
  6. Customers do not see supplier orders, cost, or batch ids. They see the order and the shipment timeline they already see.

items.text:
Who staff buy from.

Field Notes name Required email, phone Optional contact notes Optional is_active Default true

items.title: orders.ShippingLocation
items.text:
The later pack-from location for supplier goods and dispatch pickup. This is not the customer's ShippingAddress, and it is not the Warehouse already used as the order’s receiving address.

Field Notes name Required, unique code Short code used in exports, unique contact_name, phone, email Optional address_line_1, address_line_2, city, state, postal_code, country Where the supplier ships stock, and where the dispatch site collects parcels is_active Default true

items.title: Fields added to orders.OrderItem
items.text:
Copied at checkout from the product (variant's product).

Field Notes fulfillment_mode WAREHOUSE or SUPPLIER fulfillment_status See below. Default PENDING supplier FK, null. Set for SUPPLIER lines shipping_location FK, null. Set from the product

fulfillment_status:

Status Meaning PENDING Paid or not, no supplier order yet, not in a dispatch batch SUPPLIER_ORDERED Included on a supplier order that is not yet received AT_WAREHOUSE Ready to pack. Warehouse lines jump here once the order is fully paid. Supplier lines jump here when the supplier order is received EXPORTED Included on a dispatch batch that has been exported DISPATCHED Dispatch site confirmed this order shipped CANCELLED Order line will not be fulfilled

Warehouse lines stay PENDING until Order.is_fully_paid is true, then become AT_WAREHOUSE. Supplier lines stay PENDING until staff place the supplier order, even if the customer has paid.

items.title: orders.SupplierOrder and orders.SupplierOrderLine
items.text:
A staff purchase from one supplier into one shipping location. It is not a customer order.

SupplierOrder:

Field Notes supplier FK shipping_location FK. Destination of the supplier shipment status DRAFT, SENT, RECEIVED, CANCELLED reference Optional supplier reference ordered_by Staff user, null ordered_at, received_at Null until those transitions notes Optional

SupplierOrderLine:

Field Notes supplier_order FK order_item FK to the customer line. One customer line is on at most one non-cancelled supplier order quantity Copied from the customer line unit_cost Optional, from product or variant cost_price at creation. Not shown to the customer

Transitions:

  • SENT to RECEIVED sets received_at and moves those lines to AT_WAREHOUSE.

items.title: orders.DispatchBatch and orders.DispatchBatchOrder
items.text:
The handoff of one or more customer orders to the dispatch site. All orders in a batch share one shipping_location.

DispatchBatch:

Field Notes reference Generated, unique, sent to the dispatch site. Shape DB-{id} shipping_location FK status DRAFT, EXPORTED, SHIPPED, CANCELLED exported_at, exported_by Set when the payload is issued external_id Id the dispatch site returns, optional notes Optional

DispatchBatchOrder:

Field Notes batch FK order FK Unique (batch, order)

An order may sit on a batch only when:

  • is_fully_paid is true
  • status is PROCESSING
  • every non-cancelled line is AT_WAREHOUSE
  • every line's shipping_location is this batch's location
  • the order is not already on another batch in DRAFT or EXPORTED

Export (DRAFT to EXPORTED) sets each line to EXPORTED. Confirmation (EXPORTED to SHIPPED) updates the order's Shipment and sets each line to DISPATCHED. Cancelling a DRAFT or EXPORTED batch returns lines to AT_WAREHOUSE.

items.title: Confirmation
items.text:
POST /api/orders/staff/dispatch-batches/{id}/confirm/ with a staff JWT. A later shared secret can allow the dispatch site to call the same action without a staff user. The body is one order or every order in the batch.

{
  "orders": [
    {
      "order_id": 501,
      "carrier": "DHL",
      "tracking_number": "998877",
      "tracking_url": "https://track.example/998877",
      "shipped_at": "2026-10-06T12:00:00Z"
    }
  ]
}

For each order the action:

  1. Sets Shipment.status to DISPATCHED, and writes carrier, tracking number, and tracking URL.
  2. Appends a ShipmentEvent with message "Dispatched" and occurred_at from shipped_at.
  3. Relies on the existing Shipment.save to set Order.status to SHIPPING.
  4. Sets the batch to SHIPPED once every order in the batch has tracking.
  5. Sets those lines to DISPATCHED.

A follow-up delivered scan uses the existing staff shipment update: status DELIVERED. That already sets the order to COMPLETE. No second confirmation endpoint is required for delivery.

If the dispatch site cannot call the API, staff paste the same carrier and tracking into /api/orders/staff/shipments/. The batch can then be marked SHIPPED with the same side effects.

items.title: Problem
items.text: Order confirmation emails were being sent prematurely: - Sent when order was created (before payment) - Sent when payment was initiated (pending/processing status) - Not verifying payment completion before sending - Customers received confirmation emails even if they hadn't paid

items.title: Solution
items.text: Emails are now sent ONLY when payment status becomes COMPLETED.

items.title: 1. orders/emails.py
items.text:
Added payment verification: 

# Only send email if order has at least one completed payment
has_completed_payment = order.payments.filter(
    status=PaymentStatus.COMPLETED,
    is_deleted=False
).exists()
if not has_completed_payment:
    logger.info("Order confirmation email skipped; no completed payment for order %s.", order.id)
    return False

items.title: 2. orders/models.py (OrderPayment.save)
items.text:
Added email trigger on payment completion: 

def save(self, *args, **kwargs):
    # Track if status is changing to COMPLETED
    is_newly_completed = False
    if self.pk:
        try:
            old_payment = OrderPayment.objects.get(pk=self.pk)
            if old_payment.status != PaymentStatus.COMPLETED and self.status == PaymentStatus.COMPLETED:
                is_newly_completed = True
        except OrderPayment.DoesNotExist:
            pass

    super().save(*args, **kwargs)
    self._sync_order_paid_flag()

    # Send confirmation email when payment is completed
    if is_newly_completed:
        from django.db import transaction
        from .emails import send_order_confirmation_email
        transaction.on_commit(lambda: send_order_confirmation_email(self.order_id))

items.text: Removed email trigger from order creation: - Line 252: Removed transaction.on_commit(lambda: send_order_confirmation_email(order.id)) - Added comment explaining emails are sent on payment completion

items.title: 4. orders/views.py
items.text: Removed email triggers from payment creation: - Removed _queue_confirmation_email() helper method - Removed email trigger from 3 locations: - Line 213: Reusing existing payment link - Line 227: Manual payments (cash/other) - Line 288: All other payment provider workflows - Removed unused import of send_order_confirmation_email

items.title: Email Flow (New Behavior)
items.text:
1. Order Created → ❌ No email sent
  2. Payment Initiated (pending/processing) → ❌ No email sent
  3. Payment Completed → ✅ Confirmation email sent

items.title: When Payment Becomes COMPLETED:
items.text:
• Stripe webhook (checkout.session.completed)
  • IntaSend status check (check_payment_status)
  • Manual staff update via admin panel
  • Direct status update via API

items.title: Email Content Verification
items.text: The email now includes: - Order details with COMPLETED payment status - Payment invoice/reference from the completed payment - Accurate payment provider information - All order items and shipping details

items.title: Testing
items.text: Updated tests to verify: - ✅ Email sent only when payment is COMPLETED - ✅ Email NOT sent when order is created - ✅ Email NOT sent when payment is initiated - ✅ Email includes correct COMPLETED payment details - ✅ Email skipped if no completed payment exists

items.title: Benefits
items.text:
1. Accuracy: Customers only receive confirmation after successful payment
  2. Trust: No misleading emails for unpaid orders
  3. Payment Details: Email shows actual completed payment information
  4. Consistency: Same behavior across all payment providers (IntaSend, Stripe, Cash, etc.)

items.title: Cart
items.text:
This is the signed-in shopper's basket. Each person has one cart. A line is either a product or a variant, never both. Only that person can read or change it.

Base URLAuthentication 
/api/orders/cart/

You need to be signed in.

  • Each person has one cart.
  • They can only read or change their own cart.

items.title: How the storefront should keep the cart in step
items.text:
1. When the app opens and someone is signed in Call GET /api/orders/cart/me/ and replace the cart on the device with items from the response. Show subtotal and shipping_fee. Pass ?country=Kenya, or send country on sync, so shipping_fee is the fee for that destination.

  2. When they change the cart Wait a moment so you are not calling on every keystroke, then send PUT or POST /api/orders/cart/sync/ with the full list of items you want. The server replaces the cart with that list.

  3. After they place an order A successful POST /api/orders/orders/ clears the cart. Read the cart again, or trust that it is now empty.

  4. When they want an empty cart Call DELETE /api/orders/cart/clear/ if you would rather not send an empty items list.

items.title: Endpoints
items.text:
Get current cartSync cart (replace all items)Clear cart 
GET /api/orders/cart/me/

Creates an empty cart for the user if none exists yet.

Success (200):

{
  "id": 1,
  "user": 42,
  "items": [
    {
      "id": 10,
      "product": 5,
      "variant": null,
      "quantity": 2,
      "product_name": "Vitamin C 1000mg",
      "variant_description": "",
      "barcode": "",
      "unit_price": "20.00",
      "line_total": "40.00"
    },
    {
      "id": 11,
      "product": null,
      "variant": 3,
      "quantity": 1,
      "product_name": "Omega-3",
      "variant_description": "Size: 60 caps",
      "barcode": "1234567890",
      "unit_price": "15.50",
      "line_total": "15.50"
    }
  ],
  "subtotal": "55.50",
  "weight_grams": 500,
  "shipping_fee": "12.00",
  "shipping_fees": [
    { "country": "Kenya", "shipping_fee": "12.00" }
  ],
  "created_at": "2026-04-20T08:00:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-04-22T12:30:00Z"
}

Add ?country=Kenya when the shopper has chosen a destination. shipping_fee is then the fee for that country. Without it, shipping_fee is filled when only one country is configured, or when no countries are configured and the fee is 0.00. When several countries are configured and none is chosen, shipping_fee is null and shipping_fees lists each one. A country that is not on the schedule leaves shipping_fee as null and still returns the cart.

  • unit_price follows the same rule as orders: variant override price, else product price.
  • subtotal is the sum of line totals for all items.
  • shipping_fee uses the same rule as checkout: the country's unit fee when the basket is at or below that unit weight, otherwise weight divided by the unit weight times the fee. See api/shipping-rates.md.

Response fields (same object shape for GET /cart/me/, and for PUT|POST /cart/sync/ and DELETE /cart/clear/ success bodies):

Field Type Notes id integer Cart id user integer Owner user id items array Line items (see below) subtotal decimal / number Sum of line totals weight_grams integer Total product weight in the cart shipping_fee decimal string or null Fee for the chosen country, the only configured country, or 0.00 when no countries are configured shipping_fees array {country, shipping_fee} for every configured country, for this weight created_at string (ISO 8601) When the cart row was created updated_at string (ISO 8601) Last update (used for abandoned-cart timing)

Each element of items:

Field Type Notes id integer Cart line id product integer or null Product pk when line is product-level variant integer or null Variant pk when line is variant-level quantity integer Quantity product_name string Resolved product name variant_description string Option text for variants; empty for product-only lines barcode string Variant or product barcode snapshot unit_price decimal / number Price per unit line_total decimal / number unit_price × quantity 
PUT /api/orders/cart/sync/
POST /api/orders/cart/sync/

Request body:

{
  "country": "Kenya",
  "items": [
    { "product": 5, "quantity": 2 },
    { "variant": 3, "quantity": 1 }
  ]
}

country is optional. The success body uses it the same way as ?country= on GET /cart/me/.

Rules:

  • Each element must include quantity (integer ≥ 1).
  • Include product or variant, not both.
  • Duplicate product or variant IDs in one request should be avoided; the database enforces one row per product/variant per cart—prefer merging quantities on the client before sync.

Success (200): same shape as GET .../cart/me/.

Syncing also resets abandoned-cart reminder tracking for that cart (see below).

DELETE /api/orders/cart/clear/

Removes all line items. Success (200): same shape as GET .../cart/me/ with an empty items array.

items.title: Abandoned cart reminders (ops)
items.text:
The backend can email users who leave items in the cart without purchasing. Reminders are sent at 12 hours, then 24 hours, then 48 hours of cart inactivity (based on updated_at), then no further emails for that cart cycle. The cart stores that progress in last_reminder_at: empty until an email succeeds, then the cart's last activity plus the step that succeeded.

  • Template: set environment variable ZEPTOMAIL_CART_REMINDER_TEMPLATE_KEY to your ZeptoMail template key. If unset, reminder sending is skipped.

  • Background processing (django-background-tasks): reminder work runs in the DB-backed task queue, not inline in the web process.

    1. Install the package and add background_task to INSTALLED_APPS (already included in this project).
    2. Apply migrations (creates background_task tables): python src/manage.py migrate

    3. Once per environment (after deploy), schedule the repeating job:

      python src/manage.py schedule_abandoned_cart_reminders

      Interval between runs defaults to 900 seconds (15 minutes); override with env ABANDONED_CART_REMINDER_BG_INTERVAL_SECONDS.

    4. Run a worker continuously (Supervisor, systemd, etc.):

      python src/manage.py process_tasks

    Optional: queue a single run without setting up repeat (still needs process_tasks):

    python src/manage.py send_abandoned_cart_reminders

  • See the reminder queue (staff): reminder jobs live in the database. You need to be signed in as staff. This shows when the worker will run the job, not ZeptoMail's own mail queue.

    List queued / due tasks

    GET /api/orders/staff/background-tasks/
GET /api/orders/staff/background-tasks/{id}/

    Query params (list only): task_name (substring match on task_name), queue (exact), limit (default 200, max 500). Response: JSON array of task objects (list) or one object (retrieve).

    Fields on each queued task object

    Field Type Notes id integer Task row id task_name string Registered function path (e.g. orders.background_tasks.run_abandoned_cart_reminders_task) verbose_name string or null Optional display name run_at string (ISO 8601) or null Next scheduled execution time repeat integer Repeat interval in seconds (0 = no repeat) repeat_interval_label string Human label, e.g. never, hourly, or every 900 seconds for custom intervals repeat_until string (ISO 8601) or null End of repeat window, if set queue string or null Queue name attempts integer How many times execution was attempted failed_at string (ISO 8601) or null Set when the task is marked failed in-queue last_error_preview string Truncated error text (up to ~2000 chars + …) locked_at string (ISO 8601) or null When a worker claimed the task locked_by string or null Worker id (e.g. process id as string) locked_by_pid_running boolean or null Whether the locking process still appears alive status string One of: scheduled (run_at in the future), due (waiting for worker), running, failed seconds_until_run integer or null Seconds until run_at when status is scheduled; otherwise null

    List completed task runs

    GET /api/orders/staff/background-tasks/completed/

    Same query params as list: task_name, queue, limit (default 100, max 500). Response: JSON array of completed task objects.

    Fields on each completed task object

    Field Type Notes id integer Completed task row id task_name string Same meaning as queued tasks verbose_name string or null Optional display name run_at string (ISO 8601) Recorded completion / run time repeat integer Repeat interval in seconds at completion repeat_interval_label string Same as queued tasks repeat_until string (ISO 8601) or null Repeat window end, if any queue string or null Queue name attempts integer Attempt count for that run failed_at string (ISO 8601) or null If set, run ended in failure last_error_preview string Truncated error text when failed locked_at string (ISO 8601) or null Last lock snapshot locked_by string or null Last worker id locked_by_pid_running boolean or null PID check on archived row status string succeeded if failed_at is null, else failed

  • User activity: any successful sync or clear updates the cart and resets the reminder schedule for the next abandonment window.

items.title: ZeptoMail merge_info keys

items.title: Sign in with Google
items.text:
Sign in with a Google account. If we have never seen that account, we create it. You get the same access token and refresh token as a normal sign-in. You do not need to register or activate first.

EndpointAuthenticationRequest BodyFields 
POST /api/users/google-login/

You do not need to be signed in. This call is how you get the tokens.

{
  "access_token": "ya29.a0AfH6SMC..."
}
Field Type Required Description access_token string Yes Google OAuth access token

items.title: Response
Error Cases
items.text:
• Missing Token: access_token field is required
  • Invalid Token: Google access token is invalid or expired
  • No Email: Google account doesn't have an email address
  • API Error: Error communicating with Google API

items.title: How It Works
items.text:
1. Client obtains Google OAuth access token from Google
  2. Client sends the access token to this endpoint
  3. Server verifies the token with Google API
  4. Server creates or links the user account
  5. Server returns JWT tokens for authentication

items.title: Frontend (JavaScript)
items.text:
// Using Google Sign-In SDK
google.accounts.oauth2.initTokenClient({
  client_id: 'YOUR_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID',
  scope: 'email profile',
  callback: (response) => {
    const accessToken = response.access_token;
    // Send accessToken to /api/users/google-login/
  }
}).requestAccessToken();

items.title: OAuth Playground (Testing)
items.text:
1. Go to Google OAuth Playground
  2. Select "Google OAuth2 API v2" → "userinfo.email" and "userinfo.profile"
  3. Authorize and exchange for tokens
  4. Use the access token in your API request

items.title: Notes
items.text:
• If the user doesn't exist, a new account will be created automatically
  • The account is automatically activated (is_active=True)
  • If a user with the same email exists, the Google account will be linked
  • The user's profile image (image_url) is set from Google's profile picture on sign-up and updated on each Google sign-in
  • JWT tokens work the same as regular email/password login
  • The Google access token is only used for verification, not stored

items.title: Example Request
items.text:
curl -X POST https://api.endovillehealth.com/api/users/google-login/ \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "access_token": "ya29.a0AfH6SMC..."
  }'

Sign in

Sign in with an email and either a password or a short code. Do not send both. The response gives you an access token and a refresh token.

EndpointAuthenticationOption A: Password loginOption B: Code (OTP) loginFields 
POST /api/users/login/

You do not need to be signed in. This call is how you get the tokens.

{

Field Type Required Description email string Yes User's email address password string One of these User's password (use with Option A only) otp string One of these 6-digit code from email/SMS (use with Option B only)

You must provide exactly one of password or otp. Do not send both; do not omit both.

items.title: Response
Error Cases
items.text:
• Both / neither: Sending both password and otp, or neither.
  • Invalid credentials: Wrong email or password (password login).
  • Inactive account: Account is not activated.
  • Invalid OTP: Code incorrect, expired, or already used (code login).

items.title: Request login OTP
items.text:
For code (OTP) login, the client should request a login OTP first (active accounts only). ZeptoMail uses ZEPTOMAIL_OTP_LOGIN_TEMPLATE_KEY when set; otherwise ZEPTOMAIL_OTP_TEMPLATE_KEY. Merge payload includes purpose (login or activation) for template branching if needed.

EndpointAuthenticationRequest bodySuccess (200 OK)Error (400 Bad Request)

items.title: Access Token
items.text:
• Lifetime: 3 hours
  • Usage: Include in Authorization header for authenticated requests
  • Format: Bearer <access_token>

items.title: Refresh Token
items.text:
• Lifetime: 7 days
  • Usage: Use to get a new access token when it expires
  • Endpoint: /api/token/refresh/ (if implemented)

items.title: Using the Access Token
items.text:
Include the access token in the Authorization header:

curl -X GET https://api.endovillehealth.com/api/users/profile/ \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9..."

items.title: Notes
items.text:
• Use either password or code to login, not both.
  • The account must be activated (is_active=True).
  • For code login: call POST /api/users/request-login-otp/ first, then POST /api/users/login/ with the same email and the otp from the email. OTP is single-use, expires after 5 minutes, and has a maximum of 3 verification attempts.
  • Store the access token securely (e.g., in localStorage or secure cookies).
  • Use the refresh token to obtain a new access token before it expires.

items.text:

curl -X POST https://api.endovillehealth.com/api/users/login/ \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email": "user@example.com", "password": "securepassword123"}'

Code (OTP) login:

curl -X POST https://api.endovillehealth.com/api/users/login/ \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email": "user@example.com", "otp": "123456"}'

Staff only, and only while the order is PAYMENT_PENDING, PLACED, or PROCESSING.

A new line is pending. Every line must be confirmed, unavailable, or replaced before the order can move to SHIPPING or COMPLETE, and at least one line must be confirmed.

Confirm marks the line as what will ship. Optional body: { "note": "Packed" }. The note is availability_note on the line, and the customer can read it.

Unavailable keeps the line on the order, sets availability to unavailable, and leaves it out of subtotal and total. Its line_total stays so the customer can see what was dropped. Stock goes back, and the product no longer counts as sold. POST .../remove/ does the same thing. Optional body: { "note": "Supplier is out" }.

Replace keeps the original line as replaced and adds a new confirmed line for the other product or variant. The new line's replaces is the original line id. The original line's replacement is the new line id. Stock goes back on the old product and is taken from the replacement.

{ "product": 88 }

{ "variant": 14, "quantity": 1 }

The order subtotal and total are recalculated from pending and confirmed lines only. Success is 200 and the body is the full order, including every line, payments, and refunds.

When the new total is lower and the customer has a completed payment, the order includes an initiated refund for the difference. Its reason is Marked {product name} unavailable or Replaced {old name} with {new name}. The payment status becomes refund_initiated. Mark that refund completed in the Payments doc when the money has been returned. The order status stays as it was.

A more expensive replacement raises total. is_fully_paid becomes false when the payments no longer cover it. No refund is created.

quantity on replace defaults to the line's current quantity. Send product or variant, one of them.

Read status on the order. These are the values clients should handle:

Status When it is set PAYMENT_PENDING The order was just created PLACED Legacy value. Treat a paid order in this status like PROCESSING PROCESSING Completed payments cover total SHIPPING Staff record the parcel as DISPATCHED or OUT_FOR_DELIVERY, after every line is confirmed, unavailable, or replaced COMPLETE Staff record the parcel as DELIVERED, with the same line check when the order was not already shipping CANCELLED The shopper cancelled an unpaid order, or staff cancelled it REFUNDED Every received payment on a cancelled order has been refunded in full

SHIPPING and COMPLETE follow the shipment. Adding a timeline event is enough: see api/shipments.md. Setting the shipment status directly does the same. Either call returns 400 while a line is still pending, or when every line was marked unavailable. The message names the products still waiting.

Each line includes availability (pending, confirmed, unavailable, replaced), availability_note, replaces, and replacement. Unavailable and replaced lines stay in items and are left out of the total.

REFUNDED follows the refund records. Staff can also PATCH the order with { "status": "REFUNDED" }. That writes a completed refund for any balance still held and marks those payments refunded.

items.title: Payments
items.text:
Start a payment for an order, then check whether it went through.

A shopper can pay their own order with IntaSend or Stripe. Staff can record any provider, including cash.

Base URLsAuthentication
  • User payments: /api/orders/payments/
  • Check payment status (refresh from provider): POST /api/orders/payments/{id}/check-status/
  • Payment credentials (staff): /api/orders/payment-credentials/
  • Staff manage payments: /api/orders/staff/payments/
  • Staff refunds: /api/orders/staff/refunds/
  • IntaSend test connection (staff): /api/orders/payments/intasend/test/
  • Stripe webhook: POST /api/orders/payments/stripe/webhook/

You need to be signed in, except for the Stripe webhook, which Stripe calls itself.

  • Shoppers can create and read payments on their own orders. Only IntaSend and Stripe are allowed. Cash and other methods are recorded by staff.
  • Staff can create and read every payment, and the stored provider keys. Any provider is allowed.
  • Nobody can edit or delete a payment. PATCH and DELETE return 405. Returning money is a refund.

items.title: Providers and methods
items.text:
Provider Methods Notes IntaSend (intasend) link, stk Link: hosted checkout URL. STK: M-Pesa push; amount is converted to KES using currency rates. Stripe (stripe) checkout Redirects to Stripe Checkout; webhook marks payment completed. Cash / Other (cash, other) manual Staff record the payment, including status: "completed", when they create it.
  • Orders are fully paid when money still held, converted to the primary currency, is at least the order total. completed and refund_initiated payments count in full. A completed refund is subtracted. An initiated refund still counts as held.
  • If an order is already fully paid, creating a new payment returns 400 with "Order is already fully paid."
  • If an order is cancelled, creating a new payment returns 400 with "Cannot record a payment for a cancelled order."
  • Before creating an IntaSend payment, the API syncs all existing IntaSend payments for that order with the provider and blocks if the order is already fully paid. For link, if a pending link already exists, that payment is returned instead of creating a new one.

Returns a single payment (owner or staff). Use this to read the stored status; it does not call the provider.

POST /api/orders/payments/{id}/check-status/

Returns the payment and a status_check object. The provider is called only when the stored payment status is pending or processing. If the payment is already completed, failed, cancelled, refund_initiated, or refunded, the API returns the stored status without calling IntaSend or Stripe.

  • Pending/processing + IntaSend: Calls IntaSend, updates the payment record, and returns the latest status.
  • Pending/processing + Stripe: Staff or the order owner can call this. It reads the Checkout Session. A paid session marks the payment completed. An expired session marks it cancelled. The same check runs every minute for every open Stripe payment while python manage.py process_tasks is running.
  • Already completed, failed, cancelled, refund_initiated, or refunded: No provider call; returns current payment and status.
  • Other providers: Returns current stored payment and status (no provider call).

Success (200):

{
  "payment": {
    "id": 500,
    "order": 123,
    "provider": "intasend",
    "status": "completed",
    "amount": "40.00",

    "raw_provider_response": { ... },
    "created_at": "...",
    "updated_at": "..."
  },

    "is_complete": true,
    "status": "completed",
    "provider_state": "COMPLETE",
    "success": true
  }
}

Use status_check.is_complete (or status_check.status === "completed") to know if the payment is complete. If the provider call failed, status_check.success is false and status_check.error may be set.

POST /api/orders/payments/

Required: order (id), provider, method. Amount defaults to order total converted to the requested (or default) currency. You must own the order (or be staff).

IntaSend — payment link

{
  "order": 123,
  "provider": "intasend",
  "method": "link"
}

Optional: phone_number, email (passed to checkout; otherwise from order shipping address). If the order already has a pending IntaSend payment with a checkout_url, that payment is returned (201) and no new payment or link is created.

IntaSend — STK push (M-Pesa)

  "order": 123,
  "provider": "intasend",
  "method": "stk",

  • Optional: email, narrative.
  • The amount sent to M-Pesa is converted to KES using the app currency rates (products Currency table); the stored payment may use another currency for display/fully-paid calculation.

{

Before the payment is saved, open Stripe checkout sessions on that order are checked with Stripe. A paid session is marked completed. If that covers the order, this call returns 400 and no new payment is created. If an open Stripe session cannot be checked, the call returns 400 and no payment is created.

Returns 400 if the order is cancelled or already fully paid. Returns 400 if a non-empty transaction_id is already used.

items.title: Stripe webhook
items.text:
checkout.session.completed marks the related payment completed. The endpoint checks the Stripe-Signature header with STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET.

  • URL: POST /api/orders/payments/stripe/webhook/
  • Event: checkout.session.completed

The Stripe secret key is stored in Payment credentials. The webhook signing secret is environment only.

Setting Role STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET Signing secret. The webhook returns 400 until this is set. STRIPE_SUCCESS_URL Where Checkout sends the shopper after payment, when the client did not send success_url. STRIPE_CANCEL_URL Where Checkout sends the shopper if they leave, when the client did not send cancel_url.

items.title: Local development
items.text:
The storefront already sends success_url and cancel_url (/orders?payment=success and /orders?payment=failed). The two URL settings are the fallback, and for local work they point at http://localhost:3000.

Stripe cannot call your machine directly. Forward the event with the Stripe CLI while runserver is on port 8000:

brew install stripe/stripe-cli/stripe
stripe login
stripe listen --forward-to localhost:8000/api/orders/payments/stripe/webhook/ --events checkout.session.completed

stripe listen prints a signing secret that starts with whsec_. Put that value in STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET and restart runserver. Leave stripe listen running while you pay a test Checkout session. The CLI shows the delivery, and the payment becomes completed.

A deployed server uses a Dashboard webhook endpoint on the public URL instead of stripe listen, and that endpoint's own signing secret.

items.title: Refunds
items.text:
A refund is a record that money is going back to the customer. Creating or completing one does not call Stripe or IntaSend. Every refund has a reason and a transaction_id. Staff send both when they record a refund. A line change fills the reason from the change and assigns a transaction id. provider_refund_id is still optional and is the id from Stripe or IntaSend when staff have it.

Shoppers read refunds on the order (refunds on GET /api/orders/orders/{id}/). Staff list and update them here.

A refund is created in two situations:

  • Staff refund a cancelled order that has a completed payment, in full or in part.
  • Staff remove a line, or replace it with a cheaper product, on an open paid order. The API writes an initiated refund for the price difference. See api/orders.md.
ListInitiateMark done 
GET /api/orders/staff/refunds/
GET /api/orders/staff/refunds/{id}/

Staff only. Each refund has id, order, payment, status (initiated or completed), amount, currency, reason, transaction_id, provider_refund_id, initiated_by, completed_at, created_at, and updated_at.

POST /api/orders/staff/refunds/

Staff only. The order must be CANCELLED (or already REFUNDED when another payment on it still needs a refund). The payment must be completed or refund_initiated. reason and transaction_id are required. transaction_id is unique. Omit amount to refund whatever balance is still held. A smaller amount records a partial refund, and another refund can cover the rest later.

{
  "payment": 500,
  "reason": "Customer cancelled after paying",
  "transaction_id": "txn-8841"
}

Partial refund of a 40.00 payment:

{
  "payment": 500,
  "amount": "15.00",
  "reason": "One item was unavailable",
  "transaction_id": "txn-8842"
}

A later refund on the same payment can cover the remaining 25.00. amount must be greater than zero and no larger than the balance still held.

Errors:

Status When 403 The caller is not staff 400 The order is not CANCELLED or REFUNDED 400 The payment is not completed or refund_initiated 400 amount is missing when nothing is left to refund, or it is larger than the balance still held 400 reason is missing or blank 400 transaction_id is missing, blank, or already used

Success (201):

{
  "id": 9,
  "order": 123,
  "payment": 500,
  "status": "initiated",
  "amount": "40.00",
  "currency": "KES",
  "reason": "Customer cancelled after paying",
  "transaction_id": "txn-8841",
  "provider_refund_id": "",
  "initiated_by": 2,
  "completed_at": null,
  "created_at": "2026-01-20T10:00:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-01-20T10:00:00Z"
}

While any refund on that payment is initiated, the payment status becomes refund_initiated. The order stays CANCELLED. An initiated refund still counts as paid.

PATCH /api/orders/staff/refunds/{id}/

{
  "status": "completed",
  "provider_refund_id": "re_123"
}

completed_at is set. When the completed refunds cover the whole payment, its status becomes refunded. A completed refund for only part of the payment leaves the payment completed, and that part is taken out of the paid sum. When every received payment on a cancelled order is refunded, the order status becomes REFUNDED.

Creating the record with "status": "completed" records it as done in one step.

Setting the order status to REFUNDED writes a completed refund for each payment still completed or refund_initiated, and those payments become refunded.

Refunds are not deleted. Removing or replacing an order line can also create a partial refund. See api/orders.md.

items.title: Products
items.text:
This is the catalog: brands, categories, products, variants, and reviews. Anyone can read it. Only staff can change it.

A review belongs to the product, so every variant of that product shares the same reviews. avg_rating is from 0 to 5 and review_count updates itself. A review that staff have flagged is left out of both numbers.

Base URLAuthentication 
/api/products/
  • Anyone can read.
  • Only staff can create, change, or delete.

items.title: What only staff can see
items.text:
cost_price is stored on products and variants, but the response includes it only when the caller is staff. Everyone else does not receive the field.

supplier_order_urls is the same. It is a list of links staff use when they need to buy that product from a supplier. An empty list is fine. Shoppers never see it.

quantity_sold is public. It is the number of units sold, and it changes when a line is added, removed, or the order is cancelled or refunded. revenue is the sum of those line totals in the primary currency, and only staff receive it.

items.title: Prices for shoppers
items.text:
Shoppers see a price plus display_currency and currency_symbol. With no extra query, that is the primary currency, usually USD.

Add ?currency=CODE to convert. The rate is that currency's usd_rate: how many units of the currency equal 1 USD. A product stored at 10.00 USD with a KES rate of 160.25 is shown as 1602.50 KES.

Those rates stay in step with Stripe. When Stripe credentials are active, the app asks Stripe for an FX quote and saves exchange_rate as usd_rate. That is the multiplier Stripe uses to turn USD into the shopper's currency, including Stripe's FX fee, so the price on the product is the amount checkout charges. USD stays at 1. A refresh runs when a price is shown or a payment is created, and at most once an hour (STRIPE_FX_MAX_AGE_SECONDS). You can also run python manage.py update_currency_rates, or keep it repeating with python manage.py schedule_currency_rate_updates while python manage.py process_tasks is running.

rate_synced_at is when Stripe last wrote that rate. Until the first successful quote, the stored usd_rate is what shoppers see. Staff always see the price as it is stored, and still receive display_currency and currency_symbol for the primary currency.

items.title: Product Reviews
items.text:
Reviews belong to a product, and every variant of that product shares them. Someone can leave a review only after they have a completed, fully paid order whose confirmed line is that product. A line marked unavailable or replaced was not shipped, so it cannot be reviewed. The replacement product can. The rating is 0 to 5. One review per person per product. Flagged reviews are hidden from other customers and do not count toward avg_rating or review_count.

  • Create: Requires authentication and that completed order. You can submit at most one review per product.
  • Flag: Staff cannot delete a review. They flag it as PROFANITY, MALICIOUS, or OTHER (with a note). Other customers do not see a flagged review on the product or in the review list, and it does not count toward the rating. Staff and the author still see it, with is_flagged, flag_reason, and flagged_at. flag_note is staff only. The author cannot change the flag. Staff can clear it.
  • user_display: Shown as the reviewer’s first name (or "Customer" if missing). If the review is anonymous (is_anonymous: true), user_display is redacted as "Anonymous".

items.title: Shipments
items.text:
This is how a shopper follows a parcel, and how staff record each step.

One order has one shipment. The shopper reads their own. Staff can update the status and add a line to the timeline. A dispatched, out-for-delivery, or delivered update also changes the order status the shopper reads on GET /api/orders/orders/{id}/.

items.title: Base URLs
items.text:
• User shipments: /api/orders/shipments/
  • Staff shipments: /api/orders/staff/shipments/
  • Staff shipment events: /api/orders/staff/shipment-events/

items.title: Who can call these
items.text:
• Every shipment route needs a signed-in person.
  • The staff shipment routes need the Shipping role, or an admin. Orders can read shipments and cannot change them here.

items.title: What the shopper sees
items.text:
The status moves through these steps:

  • ORDER_PLACED, the order exists
  • DISPATCHED, it has left
  • OUT_FOR_DELIVERY, it is on the way to the door
  • DELIVERED, they have it

Those steps come back as events on the shipment.

items.title: What an update does to the order
items.text:
Adding an event moves the shipment forward to that event's status, and the order follows.

Event or shipment status Shipment becomes Order status becomes DISPATCHED DISPATCHED SHIPPING OUT_FOR_DELIVERY OUT_FOR_DELIVERY SHIPPING DELIVERED DELIVERED COMPLETE

DELIVERED also sets delivered_at from the event's occurred_at when delivered_at is still empty. PATCH /api/orders/staff/shipments/{id}/ with the same status values updates the order the same way.

The order stays in PROCESSING until staff have decided every line. A DISPATCHED, OUT_FOR_DELIVERY, or DELIVERED update returns 400 while any line is still pending, or when the order has lines and none are confirmed. The message names the unconfirmed products. Confirm, mark unavailable, or replace those lines first. See api/orders.md.

An event does this when it is created, and when staff change an existing event's status. An earlier status leaves a shipment that is already further along unchanged. ORDER_PLACED does not move the order.

Carrier, tracking number, and tracking URL are still set on the shipment itself. The event is what the shopper sees in events, and what moves status on the order.

items.title: Shipping rates
items.text:
Checkout sets the shipping fee. A fee sent with the order is ignored.

The fee is in USD. Each country is one row: a unit weight in grams, and the USD fee for that unit.

A basket at or below the unit weight pays that fee. A heavier basket pays (weight in grams ÷ unit weight) × fee.

Product weight is unit_weight, in grams. A variant line uses the product's weight.

Example: Kenya is 20.00 per 1000 grams. A 500 gram basket ships for 20.00. A 1500 gram basket ships for 30.00.

Until an admin adds a country, every destination pays 0.00. After at least one country is saved, checkout and quotes refuse a country that is not on the list. The message is Shipping to this country is not set.

The Orders role can still change shipping_fee on an order that has already been placed.

An admin adds a staff user and ticks the roles that person should have. A role is a Django group. An admin (is_superuser) has every role without being added to the groups.

A staff user can hold more than one role. Shoppers are not listed here.

items.text: A Django admin. Other staff receive 403.

Warehouses
items.text:
This is the address a placed order is sent to before it goes out to the customer. It is not the customer's delivery address.

Nothing is filled in for you. Until a manager or an admin adds a warehouse, new orders come back with warehouse set to null.

A new warehouse becomes the active one, and the previous active warehouse is switched off. Checkout attaches that active address to the order. Orders that were already placed keep the address they were given at the time.

items.title: Get started
items.text:
The Endoville API is how the storefront creates accounts, sells products, and ships orders. You can browse products and posts without signing in. To place an order, you create an account, sign in, and send the access token with each request.

Already building the storefront? Start here, then open the page for the area you need from the home page.

items.title: Before you start
items.text:
You need three things:

  • An email address that can receive a short code
  • A way to send HTTP requests, such as curl or Postman
  • The API base URL, https://api.endovillehealth.com

A short code is a one-time password, often called an OTP. We email it to you. It is not your account password.

items.title: Create an account
items.text: Signing in takes three calls: register, activate, then sign in. You do this once. After that you reuse the access token until it expires.

items.title: 1. Register
items.text:
Open a terminal and create the account. This does not sign you in yet. We email a short code to the address you send.

curl -X POST https://api.endovillehealth.com/api/users/register/ \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "email": "you@example.com",
    "first_name": "Ada",
    "last_name": "Okoye",
    "password": "a-long-password"
  }'

Check that inbox for the code. In these examples the code is 123456. Yours will be different.

items.title: 2. Activate
items.text:
The account stays off until you send that code back. No token is required for this call.

curl -X POST https://api.endovillehealth.com/api/users/activate/ \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "email": "you@example.com",
    "otp": "123456"
  }'

If the code expired, ask for a new one with POST /api/users/send-otp/. See OTP.

items.title: 3. Sign in
items.text:
Sign in with your email and password, or with a fresh login code. Do not send both. The response includes two tokens:

  • Access token. Send this on later requests. It lasts a few hours.
  • Refresh token. Use it to get a new access token without signing in again.
curl -X POST https://api.endovillehealth.com/api/users/login/ \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "email": "you@example.com",
    "password": "a-long-password"
  }'

items.title: 4. Call a protected route
items.text:
Put the access token in the Authorization header. The word Bearer and a space come before the token.

curl https://api.endovillehealth.com/api/users/me/ \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <access_token>"

That call returns the profile for the person the token belongs to.

items.title: Sign in with Google
items.text: If you already have a Google account, you can skip register and activate. POST /api/users/google-login/ creates the account when it does not exist yet, and returns the same pair of tokens. See Google login.
